outcome: COVID-19 infection (as an outcome for prevalence)
cohort: 550 obese pregnant women from Universitas Airlangga Hospital in 2021 were analyzed, excluding cases of incomplete data and twin pregnancies.
finding: The study found that the incidence of preeclampsia and cesarean delivery increased significantly with obesity severity, and obese women with COVID-19 had a higher risk of cesarean delivery, neonatal asphyxia, and maternal mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery incidence increased significantly with obesity severity, and obese women with COVID-19 had a higher risk of cesarean delivery.
